title: Torn Between Truth and Trust
content:
Siddu remained silent for a few moments after uttering Karthik's name.

He took another sip of his coffee before continuing.

"I was completely shocked."

"I knew Karthik."

Sneha looked at him curiously.

"You knew him?"

Siddu nodded.

"Yes. We studied together in tenth grade. We weren't very close friends, but we knew each other well enough. That's why I couldn't believe what Kiran had just told me."

He let out a slow sigh.

"My mind was flooded with questions. If Kiran was telling the truth... then why would Karthik do something like this? And if Karthik wasn't involved... then why would Kiran lie?"

"I couldn't stay there any longer, so I decided to find the answer myself."

The memory played vividly before his eyes.

"I went straight to Karthik's room."

"I didn't want him to suspect anything, so I spoke as casually as I could."

Sneha listened intently.

"I asked him, 'Hey, Karthik... do you know Shreya?'"

Siddu paused for a moment before continuing.

"He looked at me normally and smiled."

"Yeah, I know her."

"I then asked him..."

"Are you two... in a relationship?"

"Karthik immediately frowned."

"What? No."

"We're just friends. Nothing more."

He looked at me with confusion before asking,

"Besides... aren't you and Shreya in a relationship? Why are you asking me something like this?"

"I forced a smile."

"Nothing... I was just asking casually."

"After saying that, I quietly left his room."

Siddu lowered his head.

"But instead of finding an answer..."

"I only became more confused."

"My mind felt like it was being pulled in different directions."

"On one side were Kiran's words."

"On the other side was Karthik's denial."

"And above all..."

"My heart refused to stop believing in Shreya."

"I kept asking myself..."

"Who was telling the truth?"

The question refused to leave me.

"So, after thinking about it for a long time, I made a decision."

"I decided to trust Shreya."

Sneha remained silent, understanding how difficult that choice must have been.

"I went back to Kiran and told him everything."

"I said, 'I've decided to continue trusting Shreya. I don't have enough reason to doubt her. But if I ever find something suspicious with my own eyes... I won't ignore it.'"

"Kiran looked disappointed."

"He tried once again to convince me."

"But I had already made up my mind."

"He finally sighed and said,"

"I just hope you don't regret this decision someday."

Siddu's eyes drifted toward the café window.

A faint, painful smile appeared on his face.

"At that moment..."

"I thought I had made the right choice."

He paused.

"I had no idea that life was quietly preparing something far more painful than I could ever imagine."

Siddu paused for a moment, his gaze drifting toward the mountains beyond the café window.

A faint smile crossed his face, but it quickly disappeared.

"Even though I had chosen to trust Shreya," he said softly, "I still couldn't find peace."

He took a slow breath.

"She never came back to college."

"Every morning, I walked through the campus hoping today would be the day I'd see her again."

"But every evening, I returned with the same disappointment."

His voice grew heavier.

"My eyes searched for her in every classroom, every corridor, and every corner of the campus. I wasn't expecting a long conversation anymore. I just wanted to see her once... or at least receive a single message. Even a simple 'Hi' would have been enough to bring me back to life."

Sneha remained completely silent.

She could almost feel the emptiness Siddu had lived with during those months.

"The days continued to pass," Siddu said.

"One week became a month."

"Then another."

"Before I realized it, nearly three months of our second year of Intermediate had already gone by."

He lowered his head.

"By then, I had almost forgotten what it felt like to smile."

"There were days when I would return home, lock myself in my room, and cry without knowing how to stop."

"My eyes had grown tired of waiting."

"My heart had become unbearably heavy."

"My thoughts never stayed in one place."

"They wandered endlessly, just like a restless bee searching for a flower that had already disappeared."

For a brief moment, silence settled between them.

Siddu slowly looked at Sneha.

"I kept telling myself to move on..."

He gave a helpless smile.

"But how do you forget someone who still lives in every corner of your heart?"
